MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r1.claim: Mujahid says those who call on their Lord at dawn and evening are performing the obligatory prayers.

MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p375#5/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses an excessive, unrestrained affair as waste.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r3.claim: Stay with those who worship God by prayer at the two ends of the day and seek His face through prayer and fasting.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about Uyaina ibn Hisn's request to separate poor clients from him; he complained of their smell and asked the Prophet to seat the groups apart.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r5.claim: Those present included Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, Amir ibn Fuhayra, Muhja, Ayman, Abu Hurayra, and Ibn Masud; Muhja was the first martyr at Badr.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r6.claim: The Prophet is not to obey one whose heart has been made heedless of the Quran, who follows desire and lets his affair go to waste.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r7.claim: The heedless man's affair refers to his boasting about nobility and lineage; faraṭ means wasted in the Resurrection, as in 6:38.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the morning and evening remembrance with the dawn and afternoon prayers; the prescribed prayers began a year before the Prophet left Mecca for Medina.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.claim: The verse was revealed when the polytheists demanded that the Prophet dismiss Salman, Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Salim before they would sit with him; it links to a similar command.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.claim: Muʿāwiya b. Qurra interprets the command to remain with those who call on God morning and evening as referring to prayer.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.claim: The Prophet thanked God for placing in his community people with whom he was commanded to keep patient company.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.claim: The Prophet says remembrance morning and evening is better than the finest swords or freely given wealth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.claim: The Prophet tells Suraqa that keeping company with people remembering God from dawn prayer to sunrise is dearer than freeing four slaves.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.claim: The Prophet says sitting with people remembering God after the afternoon prayer until sunset is dearer than freeing eight descendants of Ishmael.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the heedless person's desire is his appetite, and Mujāhid and al-Suddī gloss his affair as waste; the phrase is linked to two verses about neglect.

FARRA:v2p139/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p139/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
FARRA:v2p139/r3.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami alone is known to have read بالغدوة; Arabic normally treats غدوة as definite without ال, as in a report meaning this morning.

FARRA:v2p139/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p139/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p139/r4.claim: ولا تعد عيناك makes the two eyes the subject: do not let your eyes turn away from the believers; the verse was revealed about Salman and his companions.

FARRA:v2p140/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p140/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p140/r1.claim: فرطا means abandoned and neglected obedience; another account says Uyayna ibn Hisn exceeded in speech by claiming leadership and nobility.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.speaker: عبد الرزاق
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.claim: Abd al-Razzaq links the command not to follow the heedless man who follows desire to Uyayna ibn Hisn.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.claim: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet praised God for making members of his community people with whom he was commanded to remain patient.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.claim: Ibrahim and Mujahid identify those who remember God morning and evening as the people of the five prayers.

AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.claim: ولا تعد عيناك uses the dual sense: your two eyes should not turn away from them.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.claim: Do not let your eyes pass beyond the poor companions to worldly adornment.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets faraṭ as regret; other interpreters say excess, with the root meaning haste and precedence.

TUSTARI:18:28/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r1.claim: Heedlessness is wasting one’s time in idleness.

TUSTARI:18:28/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r2.claim: The heart has a thousand deaths, culminating in separation from God, and a thousand lives, culminating in meeting the Real.

TUSTARI:18:28/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r3.claim: Every sin brings death to the heart, and every act of obedience brings it life.

TAB-FULL:v15p236/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r1.claim: The Prophet is to remain with companions who remember God through praise, glorification, prayer, and other good works, seeking God’s face rather than worldly gain.

TAB-FULL:v15p236/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r2.claim: The standard readers recite بالغداة; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī are reported to read بالغدوة.

TAB-FULL:v15p236/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p236/r3.claim: Arabists disfavor بالغدوة because غدوة is already definite, takes no alif-lām or genitive construction; al-Ṭabarī follows the readers’ consensus on بالغداة.

TAB-FULL:v15p237/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r1.claim: ولا تعد عيناك means do not turn your gaze from the believers to others; the expression derives from surpassing or going beyond something.

TAB-FULL:v15p237/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command as not passing over the believers for other people.

TAB-FULL:v15p237/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says some people asked the Prophet to leave the humble believers and sit with Arab nobles; the verse forbade neglecting or despising the believers.

TAB-FULL:v15p237/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف
TAB-FULL:v15p237/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl reports that after the verse came, the Prophet found poorly dressed people remembering God, sat with them, and praised God for ordering his patience with them.

TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.claim: The people whose hearts God left heedless were the unbelieving leaders who asked that the worshippers be expelled; they chose desire over obedience.

TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.claim: Khabbāb’s report identifies the leaders who sought the separation as ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r1.claim: The worldly adornment sought was status from keeping company with prominent polytheist leaders who objected to the Prophet’s poor companions.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r2.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r2.claim: A report from Khabbāb’s story says the Prophet was seen with Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, and Bilāl; visitors asked him to make the poor men leave when they arrived.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r3.speaker: عيينة بن حصن
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, before becoming Muslim, complained of Salmān’s smell and requested a separate gathering.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r4.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet praised God for placing in his community people with whom he was commanded to remain patient.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd explains زينة الحياة الدنيا here as the worldly elite.

TAB-FULL:v15p241/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r6.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
TAB-FULL:v15p241/r6.claim: Salmān reports that Uyayna, al-Aqraʿ, and their delegation wanted the Prophet to remove poor believers in wool garments so they could sit with him and learn; he found the believers remembering God and said their life and death were with him.

TAB-FULL:v15p242/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses فرطا as waste or loss.

TAB-FULL:v15p242/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r3.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r3.claim: Khabbāb’s report through al-Suddī interprets فرطا as destruction.

TAB-FULL:v15p242/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets فرطا as being opposed to the truth.

TAB-FULL:v15p242/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers waste and destruction: the careless person exceeds bounds through vanity, pride, and contempt for believers, thereby losing the truth and perishing.

TAB-FULL:v15p242/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p242/r6.claim: Asked how ʿĀṣim read the phrase, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh gives كان أمره فرطا; al-Ṭabarī adds that ʿUyayna used to boast, saying I, I.

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r2.claim: Al-Hasan rejects the idea that the callers are story-preachers; they are people who maintain the congregational prayers.

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r5.claim: Qatada interprets the morning-and-evening callers in 18:28 as the dawn and afternoon prayers.

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r6.claim: Ibn Umar says the callers in 18:28 are people who attend the prescribed prayers.

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r7.claim: Mujahid and Ibrahim identify the phrase with the five daily prayers.

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r4.claim: Abu Ja'far says the callers were people whom the Prophet taught to recite the Quran.

ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r2.claim: بالغداة والعشي is better according to all scholars because غدوة is definite and normally cannot take the article.

ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r3.claim: The believers call on God with oneness and sincerity, seeking only Him in worship.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r1.claim: Do not turn your eyes from believers toward people of status; pagan leaders asked the Prophet to distance poor freedmen, including Khabbab, Suhayb, Ammar, and Bilal.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r2.claim: The heedless person's affair was فرطا, meaning neglect and putting incapacity first.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads بالغدوة with wāw; the other readers use بالغداة.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.speaker: باقي القراء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.claim: All other readers use بالغداة without the wāw form reported for Ibn ʿĀmir.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.speaker: نصر بن عاصم ومالك بن دينار وأبو عبد الرحمن
NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.claim: They read ‘do not drive away those who call on their Lord’ with ghudwata; their evidence is the written wāw.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.claim: The orthographic wāw does not prove this reading because ṣalāt and ḥayāt are also written with wāw; al-ghudwa is normally indefinite and does not take the article.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.claim: He reads ‘do not let your eyes overlook’ with naṣb because the verb governs it.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.claim: The explanation of بالغداة والعشي is deferred to its discussion in al-Anʿām.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads al-ghudwah, treating the word as the named time without the ordinary article.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.claim: The other readers use al-ghadāh; the author considers this form clearer.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.claim: Although ghudwah is a proper name, it may be generalized and take the article; spelling it with wāw proves no wāw sound, as in الصلاة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī reads أغفلنا as 'We found him heedless,' not 'We made him heedless': if it expressed causation, the following consequence would normally use fa, not wa.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ولا تعد عينيك, a causative of 'your eyes passed beyond,' meaning turn your eyes away from the worldly adornment.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads من أغفلنا as 'one whom We found heedless,' not 'one whom We caused to be heedless'; the author defends this as an established أفعل usage and answers the theological objection.

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.claim: God commanded the wealthy to sit patiently with the poor and follow their way.

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.speaker: عمرو المكي
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.claim: Companionship with righteous, truthful poor people is a path to paradise, moving between contentment and certainty.

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم بن شيبان
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.claim: The chivalry of people of gnosis is enduring patience within the fortress of necessity alongside the patient.

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is told to remain with those who endure for God with self, heart, and spirit, who never leave the special divine presence; God likewise remains with them.

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.claim: Do not look away from them toward others, because their eyes never turn away from God.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.claim: There is beneficial heedlessness, a mercy that permits life and bodily rest, and punitive heedlessness, forgetting God and neglecting awareness that He watches.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.claim: Heedlessness is neglecting what one was commanded and forgetting God's continual blessings.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.claim: Heedlessness is following the lower self's desires.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.claim: Heedlessness is the heart's punishment and its veil from the Benefactor.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.speaker: النوري
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.claim: Heedlessness is the inner secret settling in anything other than the Real.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.speaker: ابن الجلاء
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.claim: Heedlessness is what makes a person lapse into slackness.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.claim: Heedlessness is wasting time in idleness.

THALABI:v6p165/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r12.claim: The verse was revealed when Uyayna ibn Hisn asked Muhammad to remove poor companions such as Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Amir ibn Fuhayra, Mihja, and Salman so nobles could follow him.

THALABI:v6p165/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r13.claim: The command to be patient means keep company with those who worship and revere God at dawn and evening, seeking Him rather than worldly gain or display.

THALABI:v6p165/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r14.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p165/r14.claim: Qatada interprets dawn and evening as the Fajr and Asr prayers.

THALABI:v6p165/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r15.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v6p165/r15.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar swears they are the people who perform the obligatory prayers.

THALABI:v6p165/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r16.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p165/r16.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns the seven hundred poor men of the Suffa who stayed at the Prophet's mosque, praying and waiting for the next prayer.

THALABI:v6p166/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p166/r1.claim: After the verse came down, the Prophet thanked God for giving him people with whom he was commanded to be patient.

THALABI:v6p166/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p166/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses faratan as opposing the truth.

THALABI:v6p166/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r11.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v6p166/r11.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses faratan as excess.

THALABI:v6p166/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r12.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v6p166/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses faratan as exceeding the limit.

THALABI:v6p166/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r13.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v6p166/r13.claim: Al-Farra glosses faratan as abandoned or left behind.

THALABI:v6p166/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r14.claim: Another gloss is falsehood; Abu Zayd al-Balkhi takes it as having advanced into evil.

THALABI:v6p166/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v6p166/r15.claim: Abu Ubayd relates faratan to a horse that outruns the other horses and speech that gets ahead of its speaker.

THALABI:v6p166/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r16.claim: The phrase also means that the person wasted his affairs and days; a believer uses time instead of being used by it.

THALABI:v6p166/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r2.claim: The command not to turn one's eyes away means not to look toward leaders, wealthy people, or nobles seeking worldly adornment.

THALABI:v6p166/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r3.claim: Another explanation places this gaze during the poor worshippers' seeking forgiveness and says the verse rebukes the Prophet for wanting worldly status.

THALABI:v6p166/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r4.claim: Making a heart heedless means God left it and caused it to forget His remembrance.

THALABI:v6p166/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v6p166/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the person whose heart is heedless as Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.

THALABI:v6p166/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r6.claim: Another identification names Uyayna ibn Hisn.

THALABI:v6p166/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r7.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد
THALABI:v6p166/r7.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid gloss faratan as waste or loss.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r10.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret it as the obligatory prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r11.claim: It may instead mean prayer at the day's beginning and end, seeking success in the morning and forgiveness in the evening.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r12.claim: Seeking God's face may mean doing so through supplication.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r13.claim: Alternatively, they seek God's face through their day's work; if daytime work is for God, nighttime work is even more so.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r14.speaker: اليزيدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r14.claim: Do not look past the believers toward worldly people for the sake of worldly adornment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r15.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r15.claim: The verse was revealed after Uyayna ibn Hisn, before converting, complained of Salman al-Farisi and his companions' smell and asked the Prophet to separate the groups into different gatherings.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r16.claim: أغفلنا may mean that God made the person's heart inattentive to His remembrance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r17.claim: Alternatively, God found the person's heart inattentive.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r18.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r18.claim: For people of spiritual insight, heedlessness may mean wasting time in idleness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r19.claim: Another explanation of heedlessness is excessive long-term hope.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r20.claim: A third explanation is anything that produces heedlessness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r21.claim: Following desire may mean following one's appetites and actions.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r22.claim: Alternatively, it means following a request for preferential treatment and separation from the believers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r23.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r23.claim: فرطا may mean narrow or constricted.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r24.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r24.claim: فرطا may mean abandoned or neglected.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r26.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r26.claim: فرطا may mean extravagance and excess.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r27.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r27.claim: فرطا may mean haste or rushing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r28.claim: The verb أفرط means to exceed, while فرط means to fall short.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r5.claim: اصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم means remain patiently with people who seek to magnify their Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means people who seek to obey God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r7.claim: Qatada reports that the verse came down in Medina; the Prophet praised God for making people in his community whom he was commanded to accompany patiently.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r8.claim: Calling on God morning and evening may mean supplication with hope and fear.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r9.claim: Hasan interprets the phrase as people who preserve congregational prayer.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.claim: The command says to restrain the Prophet's self rather than his heart because his heart was already with God; outward conduct is directed publicly while the heart is reserved inwardly.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.claim: The phrase about seeking God's face functions as a circumstantial expression and signals that their morning and evening invocation and intention continue without interruption.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.claim: God sheltered these seekers in worldly life through His great gifts and in the afterlife through His generous gifts; He also disclosed their hidden qualities.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.claim: Once freed from suspicion, they became free of desire for and love of every created being.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.claim: Out of reverence for the Prophet and the divine threshold, the poor did not press their request; he was told not to avert his gaze from them for worldly adornment.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.claim: The Prophet's gaze upon the poor companions serves as their means toward God and compensates them for not seeing Him until the afterlife.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.claim: The heedless include people who asked the Prophet to clear his gathering of the poor; heedlessness also means being occupied with blessings instead of their Giver.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.claim: Negligence is spending time on something other than fulfilling an obligation or performing a voluntary act.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.claim: Salmān reports that influential converts, including ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ, asked the Prophet to remove poor companions in coarse wool so they could sit near him and learn.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.claim: After finding the poor companions remembering God at the back of the mosque, the Prophet praised God for commanding him to remain patient with them, saying life and death were with them.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the warning against obeying one heedless of God was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf, who urged the Prophet to expel the poor and favor Meccan nobles; heedlessness means a heart sealed from monotheism, and desire means polytheism.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi refers readers to his fuller account of the occasion and variant reading under the passage in al-Anam.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.speaker: علي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” means do not look past them to others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.claim: The command means do not repel them with one's gaze or regard for others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as “do not turn your eyes away from them.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says not to turn one's sight toward people of status and adornment; although the eyes are addressed, the Prophet is meant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.claim: The worldly adornment sought here means company with high-status and wealthy people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.claim: “Wanting worldly adornment” is a circumstantial phrase: the Prophet is forbidden to leave poor believers while seeking elite company.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.claim: The Prophet sought chiefs' faith hoping their followers would follow; he was not accused of worldly desire, but was directed to give believers his attention and not incline toward elites. Compare the rebuke in Abasa.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.claim: “Do not obey the one whose heart We made heedless” refers to Uyaina and his father, who wanted the poor removed so they could sit with the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.claim: Muqatil glosses the word as extravagance, which may mean the excessive demand described by Ibn Abbas or the neglect described by al-Kalbi and al-Farra.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi reports Uyaina's boast that he and his people were Mudar's chiefs and that everyone would follow if they submitted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.claim: Al-Farra says Uyaina went too far by boasting that he was the Arabs' chief and they followed his religion, making his conduct excessive and boastful.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.speaker: أبو زيد البلخي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.claim: Abu Zayd al-Balkhi explains “farat” as a prior evil deed, from something that has gone ahead or occurred.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.claim: “We made his heart heedless” can mean that God left him unmarked or found him heedless, like bare land or an unvowelled book.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses “his affair was farat” as waste or loss.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.claim: Qatada says his affair was wasted in the greatest way.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes “farat” as an affair treated carelessly; al-Wahidi connects this with neglect and ruin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.claim: Al-Layth says “farat” is an affair left unattended.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.claim: Al-Farra explains “farat” as something left with obedience abandoned.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas via Ata says the man overreached in his demand and sought rank with God without piety; “farat” can derive from excess beyond bounds.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.claim: The command to stay with those who pray morning and evening is explained in al-Anʿām; he must not turn toward high-status people seeking worldly adornment or obey those who want the poor removed.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.claim: The person whose heart God made heedless abandoned faith and reflection on God's signs, following desire in a wasted and ruinous affair.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads بالغدوة والعشي with wāw and a ḍamma on ghayn in both this verse and al-Kahf; the other readers have alif and fatḥa.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the plural forms بالغدوات والعشيات; the original wāw turns into alif after fatḥa on the preceding dāl.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r7.claim: Ghaduww can mean passing beyond something; ifrāṭ is excess, while faraṭ is falling short.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r13.claim: Waṣbir nafsaka means hold yourself with the believers; they call on God at morning and evening in prayer or constant remembrance, seeking His honor and approval through worship.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r14.claim: The Prophet is told to keep his attention on the believers and not turn toward the polytheists out of desire for elite company; this does not assert he actually sought worldly adornment, and God honors the poor by preferring them.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r4.claim: The verse was revealed for poor companions including Salmān, Abū Dharr, Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, and Khabbāb when wealthy leaders demanded that the Prophet remove them before joining his gathering.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r5.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r5.claim: Another report concerns the 700 People of the Bench who stayed in the mosque between prayers; the Prophet praised God for commanding him to remain patient with them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.claim: Do not turn your eyes from poor companions toward the wealthy and eminent in pursuit of worldly adornment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.claim: God made the heart of the heedless person inattentive to remembrance; the person is identified as ʿUyayna or, by another view, Umayya ibn Khalaf.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.claim: They interpret faratan as loss or waste.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل ابن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.claim: He interprets it as excess or extravagance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.claim: He interprets it as going beyond the proper limit; Baghawī relates this to ʿUyayna's excessive claim that all people would convert if their leaders did.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.claim: Other glosses are wasting one's affairs and days, regret, falsehood, or opposition to the truth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.claim: He says the verse concerned the seven hundred poor Companions of the Bench, who lived in the mosque without trade or farmland and spent their days in prayer.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.claim: The Prophet praised God for placing in his community people with whom he was commanded to remain.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.claim: The verse was revealed when ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, before accepting Islam, asked the Prophet to dismiss poor companions such as Salman or give elites a separate gathering, promising mass conversion if he did.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.claim: The Prophet must stay with those who call on God morning and evening seeking Him alone, not worldly gain.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r1.claim: Unbelieving chiefs asked the Prophet to dismiss poor Muslims such as Suhayb, ʿAmmar and Khabbab so they could sit with him; the request resembles Noah’s people’s objection.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r10.claim: “Whose heart We made heedless” may mean God left it heedless, found it heedless, or left it unmarked by remembrance and faith; its following desire shows that compulsion is not intended.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r11.claim: A reading attaches the verb to the heart, meaning it was counted heedless; “following his desire” also describes the person’s own conduct.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r12.claim: Faratan describes one who advances beyond truth and sound judgment, casting them behind him, like a horse that runs ahead.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r2.claim: “Restrain yourself” means keep and steady yourself with the poor believers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r3.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r3.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s verse illustrates patient endurance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r4.claim: Morning and evening means constant prayer at all times; another view identifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r5.claim: A reading has “at early morning”; “at dawn” is more idiomatic because ghudwa is usually a proper name, while the article here interprets it as indefinite, an uncommon construction illustrated by poetry.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r6.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” uses ʿadā with ʿan by blending the senses of withdrawing and rising above, conveying a gaze that leaps over them toward others; compare 4:2.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r7.claim: Readings make “your eye” singular or use a causative form; a cited line with “turn away from what you see” witnesses the latter sense.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r8.claim: The Prophet is warned against despising poor believers for shabby dress and looking toward the wealthy and their finery.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670#2/r9.claim: “Seeking the adornment of worldly life” is a circumstantial clause.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.claim: Meccan leaders, or alternatively Uyayna b. Hisn and his party, asked Muhammad to dismiss poor believers such as Ammar, Suhayb, Salman, Ibn Masud, and Bilal; Ibn Atiyya prefers the Meccan leaders because the sura is Meccan.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.claim: The morning-and-evening invocation specifically means the dawn and afternoon prayers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.claim: The leaders complained that the poor companions' clothes smelled and demanded their removal before they would sit with the Prophet.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.claim: Reports say the Prophet sat with the poor believers and praised God for commanding him to be patient with them, welcoming those for whom his Lord reproached him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.speaker: سلمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.claim: Salman reports that Uyayna, al-Aqra, and their companions, described as those whose hearts were reconciled, made the same demand, prompting the verse.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.claim: The report about the reconciled leaders could make the verse Medinan, but Ibn Atiyya thinks it was likely Meccan and a reply to Quraysh.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.claim: Here ṣbir means to hold or restrain oneself; the related term describes an animal held as a target, which the Prophet forbade.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.claim: The majority read al-ghadati; Ibn Amir and several early readers read al-ghudwati, despite the latter's grammatical weakness because ghudwa is a known proper noun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.claim: The alif-lam in al-ghudwa can be explained as making the time word indefinite or generic, as in al-fina, so the reading has a possible defense.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.claim: The morning and evening invocation refers to the five daily prayers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.claim: The verse also includes people who invoke God outside prayer and those who gather to study religious knowledge.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r10.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r10.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the reading as meaning someone whom we supposed to be heedless of Us.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r11.claim: Farata may mean neglect and waste of duty, or excess and extravagance; exegetes used both senses, while Khabbab, Dawud, and Ibn Zayd gave related glosses.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet says remembering God morning and evening is better than breaking swords in God's path or freely giving wealth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman read al-ghudu without the final h; Ibn Abi Abla read the morning and evening terms as plurals.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.claim: Not turning one's eyes from the believers means not looking past them toward worldly people and the clothing of disbelievers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan's first reading uses a form that makes the Prophet the one who must not turn his eyes away; another variant has a still ʿayn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r6.speaker: خباب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r6.claim: Khabbab identifies the heedless person as Uyayna b. Hisn and al-Aqra; another interpretation takes the description generally.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the initial target is Quraysh disbelievers, since the verse is Meccan, while the wording can apply to anyone of this character.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r8.claim: The majority reading takes the heart as the accusative object: God made it heedless; another reading means that the person neglected remembrance and abandoned it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r9.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r9.claim: A variant attributed by al-Dani to Amr b. Ubayd understands the phrase as someone who neglected God's remembrance and left it.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about poor believers Salman, Abu Dharr, Suhayb, ʿAmmar, Khabbab, and others, after wealthy leaders led by ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ asked the Prophet to move them because of their smell and wool clothing.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r3.claim: After the command, the Prophet searched for the poor companions, found them remembering God at the back of the mosque, and thanked God for commanding him to stay with people who would share his life and death.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r4.claim: ‘Keep yourself with them’ means restrain yourself alongside believers who persist in prayer and supplication morning and evening, beginning and ending their days in worship.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r5.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking His exaltation and nearness, without ostentation or desire for reputation.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r6.claim: The Prophet was eager for leading polytheists to believe so their followers might follow; he did not desire worldly wealth, but was reproached for sometimes accommodating leaders and told to turn toward poor believers.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r7.claim: One reading of God making a heart heedless means He exposed it to heedlessness; the author compares it with God turning aside those who first deviated.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r1.claim: Other readings explain أغفلنا as describing a heart as heedless, finding it heedless, leaving it unmarked with the sign of believers, or abandoning it to its own course after withdrawing support; the last is attributed to al-Hasan.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r2.claim: Al-Muqatil and al-Jubbaʾi gloss فرطا as excess or extravagance; al-Akhfash says transgression beyond the limit, while Mujahid and al-Suddi say loss and ruin.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the person who neglects the beginning of an affair as one who wastes and destroys it; here the person abandons faith and proof to follow desire.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the morning term as بالغدوة, while the other readers have بالغداة; al-Hasan has a noncanonical ولا تعد عينيك and ʿAmr ibn Faʾid reads من أغفلنا قلبه.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:18:28-29/r2.claim: Abu Ali says غدوة is inherently definite like a proper name and normally takes no article, although a dialect may use it as a generic term and admit the article.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29/r3.claim: The anomalous reading ولا تعد عينيك is connected to turning the eyes away or passing beyond, as in a cited poetic use of تعدي.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29/r4.claim: On the reading من أغفلنا قلبه, the phrase may mean one whom God found heedless, supported by the cited use of أغفلت for finding someone in a state.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r1.claim: The occasion involved Uyaina ibn Hisn, Aqra ibn Habis, and others asking the Prophet to move poor wool-clad Muslims Salman and Abu Dharr away so the elite could sit close and listen.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation is waste and squandering.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r12.claim: A fourth interpretation is that his conduct was negligence or putting incapacity first.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r2.claim: The Prophet searched until he found the poor companions remembering God at the back of the mosque, then thanked God for commanding him to remain with people who shared life and death with him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r3.claim: Be patient with them by staying with them in performing the prayers at dawn and evening; the verse was explained earlier at 6:52.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r4.claim: Do not turn your gaze toward wealthy and prestigious people; the Prophet hoped their leaders' conversion would bring their followers, but he was directed toward poor believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r5.claim: Umayya ibn Khalaf asked the Prophet to expel the poor and bring Mecca's chiefs near, prompting this verse.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r6.claim: In another report, the person whose heart was made heedless is Uyaina and people like him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r7.claim: Making the heart heedless means causing it to be heedless; remembrance refers to monotheism, the Quran, and Islam.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r8.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r8.claim: He reads أغفلنا with fatḥa on lām and raises قلبه.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r9.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132#2/r9.claim: One interpretation of فرطا is excessive speech: the speaker claimed the leaders of Mudar would convert and everyone would follow.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r1.claim: The worst human state is a heart empty of God's remembrance and filled with desire that turns its attention to created beings.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r10.claim: Abu Sa'id says he sat among impoverished Emigrants, some covering one another's nakedness, while one recited Qur'an and the rest listened; the Prophet praised those he was commanded to keep company with.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r11.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r11.claim: The Prophet gave the poor Emigrants glad tidings of complete light on Judgment Day and entry into Paradise fifty thousand years before the rich.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r2.claim: God's remembrance is light and remembrance of other things is darkness: God is necessary existence and true light, while contingent beings derive from nonexistence and darkness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r3.claim: A heart lit by God's remembrance has light; turning to created beings brings darkness, so turning away from God is complete darkness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r4.claim: In this interpretation, أغفلنا describes turning away from God and واتبع هواه describes turning toward created beings.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r5.claim: One gloss of فرطا is exceeding the limit, from فرس فرط, a horse that runs ahead of the others.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r6.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r6.claim: Al-Layth says فرط describes an affair that is neglected or wasted, as in a poetic line calling an affair فرطا.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r7.claim: An unnamed poem uses فرطا to mean something wasted or neglected.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r8.claim: The phrase means that a person neglects the matter needing care, religion, and devotes his activity to worldly life.

RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p100/r9.claim: The poor believers persist in remembrance and turn away from other things, while the wealthy leaders neglect God and follow desire; the Prophet is told to stay with the former and avoid the latter.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.claim: Quraysh leaders said they would believe only if the Prophet expelled the poor, kept them away when the leaders came, and assigned the two groups separate meeting times.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r10.claim: The phrase about the eyes not passing over them forbids distancing one's gaze; عن conveys separation, as in the idiom for exceeding one's proper bounds.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r11.claim: A reading with the dual subject عينيك derives the verb from the causative or intensive forms أعداه and عداه.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r2.claim: God revealed the instruction not to expel those who call upon Him, commanding their company and honor instead of attending to the unbelievers' demands.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r3.claim: This account is a fresh, independent passage rather than a continuation of the preceding discussion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r4.claim: The parallel in al-Anam forbids expelling the poor; this verse positively commands keeping company and patiently remaining with them.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r5.claim: Sabr fundamentally means restraint; the Prophet prohibited an animal held still as a target to be shot.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r6.claim: Ibn Amir reads al-ghudwah with a damma on the ghayn; the other readers read al-ghadah, and both are Arabic forms.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r7.claim: One interpretation of morning and evening is continual observance, illustrated by a saying that someone does nothing morning and evening except insult people.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r8.claim: A second interpretation takes morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#2/r9.claim: A third interpretation sees morning awakening as a transition from death to life and evening sleep as life returning to death; the wise remember and thank God then.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r1.claim: An unnamed poetic line using عد witnesses the sense of turning away or passing over.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r2.claim: The command forbids looking down on poor believers or turning one's eyes from them to seek the company and appearance of the wealthy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p98#3/r3.claim: Wanting worldly adornment is grammatically a circumstantial accusative and means that such conduct would arise only from desire for worldly display.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.claim: A person cannot create a particular heedlessness: to intend heedlessness about a specific thing, one must conceive and thus be conscious of that thing, contradicting heedlessness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r10.claim: Razi answers that if this abandonment affects the heedlessness, the divine attribution stands; if it has no effect, it cannot explain the wording.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.claim: Trying to create undirected heedlessness is equally impossible, since it would not explain why one becomes heedless of one object rather than another.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.claim: Because a servant cannot produce heedlessness in himself, God must be the creator of heedlessness, and أغفلنا denotes creation rather than merely finding.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.claim: The objection from the waw assumes that creating heedlessness necessarily causes desire-following; it does not, since a heedless person may remain hesitant, bewildered, or afraid.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal offers a Mu'tazili reading in which God showered worldly goods on them, causing their hearts to become heedless.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r6.claim: Razi replies that if worldly pleasures affect their heedlessness, God caused it by giving them; if they do not affect it, the attribution fails.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal also glosses أغفلنا as leaving the person heedless without marking him with the sign of purity and piety, like an unmarked camel.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r8.claim: Razi says this gloss is equivalent to saying God blackened the heart or whitened the face and therefore does not escape his argument.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p99#2/r9.claim: A third al-Qaffal interpretation is that God left the heart with Satan and did not prevent Satan from reaching it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r1.claim: Asharites cite God saying that He made the person's heart heedless as evidence that God creates ignorance and heedlessness in such hearts.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r10.claim: The causative sense is also preferable because knowing a thing depends on its coming to exist; making the form literal for the prior event and figurative for cognition follows that relation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r2.claim: The Mu'tazila read the wording as God finding the heart heedless, not creating heedlessness in it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r3.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب الزبيدي
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r3.claim: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib illustrates the found-such wording by saying his opponents were not found cowardly, miserly, or unable to answer satire.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r4.claim: Their first objection is that creating the heedlessness would remove the person's entitlement to blame.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r5.claim: Their second objection cites the following invitation to believe or disbelieve: it would not make sense if God had created the heedlessness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r6.claim: Their third objection says that if God caused heedlessness, following desire should be connected by fa as a consequence, like breaking followed by breaking, rather than by waw.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r7.claim: Their fourth objection is that if God truly made the heart heedless, the act should not be attributed to the person's following his desire.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r8.claim: In answer, the Mu'tazila restate that أغفلنا means that God found the heart heedless rather than producing its heedlessness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p99/r9.claim: The verb pattern أفعل is more properly taken as bringing something about than as finding it: causative usage is more frequent and more readily understood.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r1.claim: Those seeking God’s face are seeking His obedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning about the heedless heart was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf, who wanted the poor kept away and Meccan nobles brought near; heedlessness means a heart sealed against monotheism.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r11.claim: Following one’s desire here means shirk.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r12.claim: Faraṭ may mean negligence and falling short through delaying faith, excess beyond bounds in boastful speech, or being first to do evil.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r13.claim: The phrase God made his heart heedless may mean that He found it heedless, as in ordinary Arabic expressions that describe finding someone in a condition.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r14.speaker: عبد الرزاق وسفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r14.claim: An alternative occasion identifies the heedless person as Uyaina ibn Hisn al-Fazari.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r2.speaker: نصر بن عاصم ومالك بن دينار وأبو عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r2.claim: These readers recite the parallel command as do not expel those who call on their Lord at morning and evening, citing its spelling in the codex.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas says the codex spelling does not compel that reading, since life and prayer are also written with waw, and Arabs rarely say al-ghudwa because the time is already familiar.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r4.claim: Hasan’s reported reading says do not let your eyes pass beyond them; al-Yazidi explains it as looking toward worldly people instead.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is not to look down on the poor, as when an eye recoils from someone it regards as contemptible.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is told not to seek the adornment of worldly life by keeping company with the leaders who wanted the poor removed; he did not intend to do so, but God forbade it as a warning despite His protection of him from shirk.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r7.claim: Tureed is a present-tense circumstantial verb, illustrated by Imru al-Qays’s use of a present verb in a circumstantial setting.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r8.claim: Against the claim that the verb must govern the eyes directly, the author explains the raised eyes as equivalent to their not turning away, with the command in meaning directed to the Prophet.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj clarifies that the command means not to turn the Prophet’s gaze from the poor toward people of status and adornment.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r1.claim: Salman reports that Uyaina ibn Hisn and al-Aqra ibn Habis asked the Prophet to move poor wool-clad Muslims such as Salman and Abu Dharr away so the notables could sit and learn from him.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:28/r2.claim: The passage from the recitation command through the warning of Hell was revealed in response; the Prophet found the poor worshippers remembering God and praised the command to stay with them in life and death.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.claim: The command is to hold oneself firmly with those who invoke God at the gathering times or at the day's two ends; Ibn Amir reads the form as al-ghudwa.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking His approval and obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.claim: Do not let your gaze pass over the poor believers, turning away from their shabby clothes in desire for wealthy people's finery; the construction embeds the sense of turning away.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.claim: The phrase is also read with the dual eyes or with a form derived from causing the eye to pass beyond them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.claim: The person whose heart was made heedless is identified as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who urged Muhammad to expel poor believers for Quraysh's leaders.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.claim: Mu'tazilites reject the apparent divine attribution of heedlessness, suggesting God found the heart so, attributed it to the person, or left it unmarked; the author answers with his previous arguments.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.claim: Following desire means the person's affair is excessive, advancing past truth and casting it behind his back; the root also describes a horse that runs ahead.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r1.claim: The verse came after Quraysh's leaders asked the Prophet to dismiss poor Muslims such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, and Salmān before they would sit with him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r2.claim: Stay with those who invoke their Lord continually; morning may be for asking success and ease, evening for pardon of shortcomings, or the times may mean Fajr and ʿAṣr.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r3.claim: The Syrian reading has the form al-ghudwah; those devoted to worship seek God's pleasure.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r4.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” combines the sense of passing over and eyeing them with aversion; this semantic inclusion strengthens the expression.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r5.claim: The phrase “desiring the adornment of worldly life” is circumstantial.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r6.claim: “Whose heart We made heedless” supports the author's doctrine that God creates human acts.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#4/r7.claim: The heedless person follows desire, and his affair exceeds the bounds of right.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.claim: Patience with God’s people is steadfastness and empowered presence through God, with no attention turned elsewhere.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.claim: Those invoking God morning and evening are stripped poor who seek only His essence, without worldly or afterlife needs or fixation on acts and attributes.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.claim: Morning and evening signify annihilation and abiding; looking away from these seekers means turning attention toward anything other than God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda consider the verse commanding patience with the worshippers a Medinan exception to the otherwise Meccan sura.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.claim: One occasion report says Quraysh offered to sit with the Prophet if he dismissed poor followers such as ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Salmān, Ibn Masʿūd, and Bilāl, complaining about the smell of their clothes.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.speaker: سلمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.claim: Salmān reports that ʿUyayna b. Ḥiṣn, al-Aqraʿ, and other reconciled leaders made the request, which would make the verse Medinan; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the Quraysh report because the sura is Meccan and their behavior matched it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.claim: اصبر نفسك means keep yourself with them and remain steadfast; the command shows special care for these companions, with مع requiring companionship and shared company.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s verse about a noble woman holding steady while a coward’s breath rises illustrates the sense of صبرت as enduring steadfastly.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.claim: A prophetic report forbids ṣabr of an animal, meaning tying it up as a target for shooting; this shows the word’s sense of restraint.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, and Ibrāhīm take morning and evening as the five daily prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.claim: Qatāda specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.claim: He also allows the phrase to mean constant worship generally, as ‘striking front and back’ can refer to the whole body rather than only those parts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.claim: Where ordinary wording supports the meaning, Abū Ḥayyān prefers its lexical sense over an added semantic incorporation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.speaker: الرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.claim: The Muʿtazilī al-Rummānī says God did not mark the heart with the signs given to believers, likening it to an unbranded camel or unvowelled book.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān contrasts Sunnī teaching: God truly made the person heedless and creates the misguidance and heedlessness within him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.speaker: المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal glosses أغفلنا as leaving the person empty of remembrance, meaning the Qurʾān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ likewise treats the doubled form as transitive, as with the hamzated reading.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Basran grammarians accept this kind of semantic incorporation only under necessity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ولا تعد from the hamzated form أعدى; another report from him, ʿĪsā, and al-Aʿmash has doubled ʿayn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and the author of al-Lawāmiʿ claim hamza or doubling makes the verb transitive, citing the verse فعد عما ترى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.claim: He rejects that analysis: hamza and doubling here do not add transitivity, since the base verb is already transitive and only one object appears.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا as a circumstantial clause.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.claim: If the possessor is the dual عيناك, the verb should be تريدان; if it is the Prophet, a circumstance attached to a genitive pronoun has a syntactic difficulty, though some allow it when the possessed noun is part-like. The eyes stand for the Prophet’s looking.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives Muʿtazilī readings of من أغفلنا قلبه: God made or found the heart heedless, or left it unmarked by remembrance like an unbranded animal or unvowelled book; he also links this to hearts not given faith.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.claim: The people whose hearts were made heedless are apparently Quraysh, whose disbelief and prevailing wretchedness occupied their hearts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.claim: Ibn Baḥr takes faratan as something immediate and swift, citing the description of man as hasty.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.claim: Other transmitted glosses of faratan are regret and falsehood.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets faratan as opposed to the truth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
