ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows faratan to mean either neglecting what one should keep to or excess and extravagance in one's course and desire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.claim: He prefers Quraysh over the proposed identifications with ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ because the verse is Meccan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.speaker: عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.claim: They read aghfalnā with the lām open and qalbahu with the bāʾ damma, syntactically assigning the action to the heart.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.speaker: ابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the variant as meaning that God found them heedless of the heart.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses the variant as finding the heart heedless, from the verb meaning to find someone heedless.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.claim: They interpret faratan as loss and waste.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān reads faratan as excess or extravagance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ understands faratan as abandoned or neglected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses faratan as going beyond the proper limit.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r1.claim: Poetic usages by Imru al-Qays and another poet support treating the paired eyes as a single grammatical unit; attributing desire to the eyes is metaphorical.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says تريد is a circumstantial clause; the Shaykh asks whether its subject is عيناك, which would require the dual تريدان.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r3.claim: If the circumstantial subject is the addressee expressed by the possessive ك, the genitive possessor and clause have different governing factors; some allow this when the possessed thing is a part or near-part.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r4.claim: The author proposes تعد as predicated of the addressee, with عيناك as a part-for-whole بدل from the pronoun.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#2/r5.claim: تريد can be circumstantial from either عيناك or the pronoun in تعد, though the latter is weaker because agreement rarely follows a replaced pronoun; a poetic line illustrates the exception.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r1.claim: The common reading makes نا the subject of أغفلنا and قلبه its direct object.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r2.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد بن فائد وموسى الأسواري
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r2.claim: They read أغفلنا with fatḥa on lām and قلبه as nominative, assigning the heedlessness to the heart.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r3.speaker: ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the unusual construction as meaning that We thought him heedless of it.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets it as We found his heart heedless.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa offers two readings: finding the heart turned away, or neglecting the matter of remembering Us.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r6.claim: فرطا may be an adjective like a horse that runs ahead, meaning this person's conduct precedes the truth.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:28#3/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya says فرطا may mean neglect and waste, or excess and extravagance.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r1.claim: واصبر نفسك means restrain and steady yourself; Abu Dhuayb's verse witnesses the sense of صبرت.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r10.claim: تريد is circumstantial; its subject may be the addressee or the two eyes, with singular agreement allowed for closely linked things.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r2.claim: One parse supplies the omitted object of تعد as النظر: do not let your eyes pass over looking at them.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says عن is licensed because عدا is used with the sense of نبا or علا, yielding the combined meaning of looking past and rejecting them.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the purpose of the semantic extension as combining two meanings, stronger than either alone, and compares 4:2.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r5.claim: The Shaykh objects that Basran grammar does not treat semantic extension as productive and permits it only under necessity.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r6.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reads عينيك with a plural verb form derived from the quadriliteral أعدى.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r7.speaker: الحسن وعيسى والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r7.claim: These readers use the doubled form تعد, deriving it from the intensified verb عدى يعدي.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r8.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو الفضل
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Fadl attribute the transitivity in these readings to hamza or doubling and cite a line by al-Nabigha for عدا.

SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:28/r9.claim: The Shaykh argues that if hamza or doubling caused transitivity, the verb should take two objects; the cited authors already acknowledge عدا بمعنى جاوزه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r4.claim: The Prophet should sit with people who remember, praise, glorify, and invoke God morning and evening, regardless of whether they are poor or rich, strong or weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r5.claim: It is said that Quraysh notables asked the Prophet to meet them alone and separate from poor companions such as Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ibn Masud; God instead commanded him to remain with them, as in 6:52.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r6.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r6.claim: Sa'd recounts that six companions were with the Prophet when polytheists demanded that he dismiss them; he felt what God willed, and this verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed. Muslim alone transmits it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r1.claim: The Prophet told a preacher to continue, saying that sitting from morning until sunrise listening to him was dearer than freeing four people.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r2.speaker: رجل من أصحاب بدر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r2.claim: A man from the veterans of Badr heard the Prophet say that sitting in a preacher's gathering was dearer to him than freeing four people; Ahmad transmits the report through Kurdus.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r3.claim: The Prophet preferred sitting with people remembering God from dawn prayer to sunrise over everything the sun shines on, and remembrance from afternoon prayer to sunset over freeing eight descendants of Ishmael, each valued at twelve thousand; Anas corrects a report that says four, totaling their value as ninety-six thousand.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p152/r4.claim: When the Prophet passed a man reciting the Cave or Hijr and the man stopped, he said this was the gathering in which he had been commanded to remain patiently; al-Bazzar gives both a disconnected route and a connected version from Abu Hurayra and Abu Sa'id.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r1.claim: A group who gather to remember God seeking only His face are called from heaven to rise forgiven, with their bad deeds changed into good; Ahmad alone transmits this report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r2.claim: When this verse came while the Prophet was at home, he sought out rough, poorly clothed people remembering God, sat with them, and praised God for making such people part of his community; al-Tabarani transmits the report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p153/r3.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud listed Abd al-Rahman as a Companion, while his father was among the leading Companions.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r1.claim: Do not look past the poor worshippers toward others in search of people with social rank and wealth.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p154/r2.claim: The heedless person is occupied with worldly life instead of religion and worship; his affairs are folly, neglect, and waste, so do not obey, love, or envy his way. The warning recalls not coveting worldly adornment in 20:131.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.claim: The Prophet was grieving over unbelievers, while leaders offered to listen if he expelled poor believers such as Ammar, Suhaib, and Bilal.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.claim: He must remain with believers who call on God morning and evening seeking His face alone, even if they are socially poor.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.claim: He must not turn toward worldly adornment or obey those whom God has made heedless, who follow desire and exceed all bounds.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.claim: The author reads أغفلنا as God's action: He caused the heart to be heedless, and the consequent loss of remembrance leaves darkness for desire to fill.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.claim: The followers will be rescued and raised over tyrants as the cave sleepers were, because they turn to God and away from everything else.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.claim: Influential men asked the Prophet to exclude poor Muslims such as Salman and Abu Dharr and seat the chiefs instead; revelation of the passage threatened them with Hell.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.claim: The Prophet searched for the poor worshippers in the back of the mosque, found them remembering God, and praised God for commanding him to remain with them in life and death.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.claim: A man wearing a coarse cloak shoved Salman aside and asked the Prophet to keep the poor away when elites visited; the verse commanding patience with them was revealed.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.claim: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet found ragged, humble people remembering God, sat with them, and praised God for including them in his community.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة وأبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.claim: When a man read al-Hijr and al-Kahf, the Prophet identified the gathering as the one in which he was commanded to remain.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.speaker: عمر بن ذر
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.claim: When Abdullah ibn Rawaha stopped reminding his companions upon the Prophet's arrival, the Prophet told him to continue and called them the gathering with whom he was ordered to remain.

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.claim: Mujahid transmits Ibn Abbas's report of the Prophet telling Abdullah ibn Rawaha that his companions were the assembly God commanded him to remain with.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.claim: A report continues that angels attend gatherings where God is remembered, mirror the worshippers' praise, then God forgives the group, including a sinful companion, since no one sitting with them is deprived.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.claim: The Prophet asked a preacher to continue; sitting in the morning until sunrise, he said, was dearer than freeing four slaves.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.claim: The Prophet told poor Muslims with a Quran reciter to rejoice in complete light on Judgment Day and enter Paradise five hundred years before the wealthy, who will be reckoned.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.speaker: ثابت
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.claim: When Salman and others stopped remembering God as the Prophet approached, he asked them to continue, saying he had seen mercy descend and wanted to share it.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.claim: A heavenly caller announces forgiveness and the replacement of sins with good deeds for people who gather solely to remember God.

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.claim: Ibn Umar says those addressed by the command to remain with worshippers are people who attend the obligatory prayers.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the people of remembrance as worshippers who attend the obligatory prayers.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.claim: The verse refers to the dawn and afternoon prayers.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.speaker: عبيد الله بن عدي بن الخيار
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.claim: The people with whom the Prophet should remain are Quran reciters.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command not to obey the heedless was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf's demand that the poor be dismissed and Meccan chiefs brought near; heedlessness means a heart sealed against monotheism, and following desire means idolatry.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.speaker: ابن بريدة
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.claim: Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to exclude Salman because of the smell of his wool garment when elites visited; the verse was revealed.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.claim: Al-Rabi says the Prophet turned from distracted Umayya ibn Khalaf after the verse was revealed, then found Salman remembering God and praised those he was commanded to remain with.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.claim: Ibrahim identifies the morning and evening worshippers as people of remembrance.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.claim: Ibrahim says not to drive the worshippers away from remembrance.

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.claim: The Prophet was commanded to stay with his companions and teach them the Quran.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says those who call upon their Lord are those who worship Him.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.claim: The instruction not to let one's eyes pass beyond them means not to look away from them toward others.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.speaker: أبو هاشم
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.claim: Abu Hashim says they would compare or distinguish one another regarding lawful and unlawful matters.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr also connects the verse with distinctions concerning lawful and unlawful matters.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.claim: Ibrahim and Mujahid identify the worshippers as those who perform the five daily prayers.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed after Uyayna ibn Hisn asked for a separate gathering because Salman smelled bad to him.

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses فرطا as loss or waste.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.speaker: خباب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.claim: The same report says the Prophet would leave the poor believers when he stood, after which the instruction to keep himself with those who call upon their Lord was revealed.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.speaker: خباب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.claim: The occasion for “keep yourself with those who call upon their Lord” was already given in the account from Khabbab in Surah al-An'am.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the instruction not to obey one whose heart is heedless concerned Umayya ibn Khalaf, who wanted the Prophet to expel the poor and favor Makkan leaders.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.speaker: الربيع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the Prophet turned his attention to Umayya ibn Khalaf, who was inattentive to what he was being told, and the verse was revealed.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Uyayna ibn Hisn entered while Salman was with the Prophet and demanded that Salman be removed when Uyayna's party arrived; the verse was revealed.

BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.claim: The command means to restrain and steady oneself in the companions' company; morning and evening can mean constant supplication, or seeking success in the morning and pardon in the evening.

BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.claim: Unbelieving chiefs demanded that Muhammad expel poor companions such as Suhayb, ʿAmmār, and Khabbāb, citing their smell and low status and promising mass conversion if he sat with elites; Noah's people made a similar complaint.

BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.claim: Though expelling a few companions might seem a lesser harm than keeping the chiefs in disbelief, someone who refuses faith because of poor company is a hypocrite, so his demand deserves no regard.

BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.claim: Given the dignity of prophethood, expelling believers for an uncertain prospect would be grave wrongdoing; such exclusion belongs to worldly rulers, while religious leaders attend to inward states.

BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.claim: Seeking God's Face means seeking His pleasure, not a worldly benefit; the metaphor connects approval to the face where approval and anger are manifest.

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.claim: Following desire leads to ruin; the chiefs' opposition arose from heedless hearts occupied with fleeting falsehood, while honor lies in pure hearts and inner character, not outward beauty.

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.claim: His couplet says spiritual ascetics would not buy the satin robe of someone devoid of virtue.

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.claim: A hadith says God looks at hearts and deeds rather than forms and wealth; good hearts and acts bring acceptance regardless of appearance or riches.

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.claim: A story says angels questioned Abraham's suitability as intimate friend amid his attachments; God tested him through Gabriel, who offered to buy his twelve gold-collared dogs and flock. Abraham repeatedly let him take more, then gave all freely, refusing to revoke the gift when Gabriel disclosed himself. God directed him to sell them and endow the proceeds, which funded the shrine's endowment.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.claim: Do not let your gaze pass beyond the poor companions; the eyes are the grammatical subject, while the command addresses their owner and warns against disdaining their worn clothing to seek the rich.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.speaker: ذو النون
BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.claim: He reads the verse as God's admonition to remain with those who stay at the divine presence morning and evening; those whose eyes never turn from God deserve that the Prophet never turn from them.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.speaker: زبدة التفاسير
BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.claim: It treats تريد as oriented to the future, not a judgment that the Prophet desired worldly adornment; he warned against worldly life and the rich. Al-Kashifi says he never desired it; the point is not to act that way.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.claim: Do not obey those demanding the poor be removed; heedlessness prevents grasping realities, and God made the Quraysh chiefs heedless of remembrance.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.claim: Hawāʾ first means what the self loves and came to denote blameworthy desire opposed to religious law; an act is attributed to a servant by capacity and to God by creation.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.claim: The lexicon says farat can mean injustice, aggression, or an affair exceeding its limit; here the chiefs leave truth behind, like a horse ahead of the herd.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.claim: “Restrain yourself” means hold someone in place, as in the prohibition against confining an animal for target practice; applying it to steadfast endurance is an extended use, not the literal sense, because the verb's transitivity differs.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.claim: One reported occasion is that Quraysh chiefs, including Umayya ibn Khalaf, offered to listen if the Prophet moved poor believers away because their wool garments smelled.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.speaker: سلمان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.claim: A report from Salmān says the influential converts ʿUyayna ibn Badr and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis asked the Prophet to sit at the head of the assembly and send away Salmān, Abū Dharr, and the poor Muslims in wool garments so they could listen and learn.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.claim: The reports disagree about the verse's setting: the Quraysh account makes it Meccan, while the Salmān report makes it Medinan; Abū Ḥayyān prefers Meccan because the surah is Meccan, but al-Ālūsī says most reports support Medina and such verses can be exceptions.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.claim: A report through Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk attributes the Meccan occasion to Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Ālūsī says the verses that follow may favor the Medinan setting.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.claim: The relative description “those who call their Lord” explains the order to remain with them: their defining devotion warrants continued companionship.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads “in the morning” with the definite article. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl explain this through Arabs' use of the word as an indefinite noun; al-Raḍī says it can be indefinite by agreement, although it is usually a declinable-proper genus name.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.claim: Some verifiers prefer the first grammatical explanation because making a genus name indefinite is less clear than making a personal proper name indefinite; al-Fannārī objects to treating the month name Rajab this way, and al-Ālūsī leaves the discussion to its proper place.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.claim: This verse is more emphatic than the parallel command not to drive away those who call upon God morning and evening.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.speaker: السهيلي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.claim: “Seeking God's face” means seeking His pleasure and approved obedience, not display or fame; al-Suhaylī explains the metaphor through the turning toward someone one favors and turning away from someone one resents.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.claim: Alternative readings take “face” as God's essence with an omitted genitive, or as turning toward Him and seeking nearness; al-Ālūsī prefers the first, pleasure-based interpretation.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.claim: Being with the people means keeping their company; calling upon God morning and evening is a common way to express constant worship, like saying someone struck morning and evening to mean the whole body.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.claim: Some keep morning and evening literal rather than treating them as all times; these times are singled out because people are distracted by work and are prone to heedlessness.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.claim: The worship in question is remembrance of God, reported from Ibrāhīm through Mughīra.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.speaker: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.claim: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār is reported to say the worship is recitation of the Quran.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr says it means discussing lawful and unlawful matters.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Mujāhid identify the worship as attending the five daily prayers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.claim: Qatāda specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers; al-Ālūsī says the preceding discussion supports the apparent, literal times.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.claim: The people meant are poor Companions, including ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Salmān, Ibn Masʿūd, and Bilāl.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.claim: “Seeking worldly adornment” means seeking the company of wealthy worldly people unlike the poor believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.claim: “Do not obey” prohibits removing the poor from the Prophet’s gathering at the urging of the heedless elite.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.claim: God made the elite’s hearts wholly unprepared for remembrance; their heedlessness contrasts with the poor who invoke God morning and evening.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.speaker: المفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.claim: Al-Mufaddal interprets remembrance here as the Qur’an.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.claim: On the canonical reading the clause is circumstantial, most naturally attached to the eyes in عيناك; the genitive relation can license that attachment.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashf assigns the circumstantial clause to the preceding verb, as in the construction بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.claim: The singular “you seek” can be attributed to the eye as a metonym for its owner’s desire; it may also mean looking for play rather than reflection.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.claim: The eye is treated as singular because perception is one, to signal its rhetorical insertion, or because the paired eyes are one bodily organ.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.claim: The author finds the ordinary circumstantial reading sound under either explanation of تعد; objections to a circumstantial clause from a genitive are too weak to displace it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.claim: Some assign the clause to the genitive only when تعد means passing beyond, and to the governing noun when it means turning away; the author sees this as stylistic preference.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.claim: If turning away is meant, attaching desire to the eye keeps the sentence’s beginning and end parallel and avoids directly attributing worldly desire to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.claim: On the two anomalous readings, the clause is circumstantial from the hidden subject of the verb.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.claim: The command forbids turning attention from the poor believers toward worldly people; its purpose is to prevent scorning them for their shabby condition.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.speaker: الزمخشري وصاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.claim: They treat the hamza and doubling in these readings as causative morphology.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan says that analysis fails: since the base verb already takes an object, causative morphology should yield two objects, which these readings lack.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.claim: He reads عدا as “turn away,” with the verb taking the person or thing turned from as its second complement through عن.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.claim: An alternative lexical construction gives عدا one object with عن, meaning to pass over or leave something.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.claim: Raghib says عدا intrinsically means passing beyond; Zamakhshari therefore supplies the sense of recoiling or rising above the object to explain عن.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.claim: Zamakhshari argues that the wording combines leaving the believers and recoiling from them, a stronger effect than a single sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that Arabic-style verb inclusion is not analogical and should be used only from necessity when the ordinary lexical sense works.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.claim: The further objection that a semantic synonym must share the same transitivity is not compelling; the lexicon supports the alternative reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb lightly as أعداه, with the eyes as an accusative object.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.speaker: عيسى والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.claim: Isa and al-Aʿmash read the doubled verb عَدَّاهُ, likewise with the eyes in the accusative.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.claim: The verse’s apparent wording supports the Sunni doctrine that God makes the heart heedless; Muʿtazilites reinterpret it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.claim: An objection says removing the poor might secure elite conversion, making a small injury preferable to the greater harm of continued unbelief.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.claim: God knew the elite would at most make a merely outward profession, insufficient reason to violate the honor of the righteous poor.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.claim: The well-known Muʿtazilite interpretation takes “We made his heart heedless” as God’s abandonment or withdrawal of aid.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.claim: Interpreting the phrase as “We found him heedless” is objectionable because it suggests God stumbled upon the state without prior knowledge.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.speaker: الكميت
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the verb as “attributed heedlessness to him,” illustrated by al-Kumayt’s line about people calling him wrong or sinful.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.speaker: الرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.claim: Al-Rummani says God did not mark the heart with remembrance as a sign of faith, using the image of an unmarked animal; the author calls it subtle but contrary to the apparent sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.claim: They argue that “he followed his desire” assigns the act to the servant, and that a divinely caused sequence should have used a causal فَـ.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.claim: Human acts may be attributed to the servant through acquisition and power and to God through creation; omission of a causal particle can be rhetorically deliberate.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.speaker: عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.claim: They read أَغْفَلْنَا with fatḥa on ف and ل and قلبه nominative, making the heart the subject: “we found it heedless.”

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.claim: On that reading, the sense is that God supposed them heedless, with remembrance of God used as a metonym for divine requital.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.claim: God may also have forbidden expulsion because humiliating early believers would alienate hearts, prompt recent converts to apostatize, and deter future entrants.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.claim: This potential damage to Islam outweighs leaving a small group of unbelievers in their disbelief.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.claim: Mujahid explains فرطا as waste and ruin.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes فرطا as having advanced past truth and right, leaving them behind.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows فرطا to mean either neglect and waste of religion or excess and extravagance; Muqatil likewise glosses it as extravagance.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.claim: Muqatil explains the word as excess and extravagance.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.claim: Calling the elite “those whose hearts We made heedless” signals that their heedlessness and appetite explain why they must not be obeyed.

ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.claim: Those who pray morning and evening are rendered as seeking their Lord's beauty; the Prophet is told not to turn his eyes away from them for worldly adornment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.claim: Meccan leaders said they would listen if poor believers and slaves were removed; God answered this demand at 6:52 and more forcefully here by ordering the Prophet to stay with them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.claim: Iṣbir nafsaka means keep yourself continually with them; ṣabr conveys staying fixed, and the verb takes maʿa because it includes the sense of companionship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.claim: Al-ghadāh is the time between dawn and sunrise, and al-ʿashī is evening; their prayer and supplication encompass the day and night, including formal prayers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads bil-ghudwah with sukūn on dāl and a wāw, a synonym of al-ghadāh.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.claim: Calling them ‘those who pray’ hints that their devotion makes them especially worthy of companionship; ‘seeking His face’ figuratively means seeking God’s favor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.claim: The apparent command not to let the eyes pass them means not to look away or ignore them; addressing the eyes themselves is an elegant compression for addressing their owner.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.claim: ‘Wanting worldly adornment’ describes the addressee’s state; desire for status or appearance must not cause him to leave companions lacking outward finery.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.claim: The verse exposes the elites’ foolish fixation on appearances and their contempt for people of virtue, sound minds, and enlightened hearts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.claim: The prohibition establishes a broad rule for the Prophet and Muslims in responding to polytheists’ demands and ends their hope of obtaining concessions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.claim: The indefinite ‘whoever’ can apply generally to anyone matching the description; another report says the verse concerned Umayya ibn Khalaf asking that poor Muslims be expelled.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.claim: Making a heart heedless means its constitution leaves it inattentive to divine unity so polytheism takes root; these people have weak insight and are driven by habit and desire.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.claim: The persistent heedlessness is innate, while following desire is a chosen act; the two clauses distinguish created disposition from human agency.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.claim: Furaṭ means injustice and aggression, derived from going ahead because wrongdoing rushes into evil; amr means condition, and kāna marks its entrenched state.

TABATABAI:18:28-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects treating the verse as proof that God compels people to sin; punitive constraint follows their choices.

TABATABAI:18:28-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r2.claim: Punitive constraint does not negate free choice; only constraint imposed initially would do so.

TABATABAI:18:28-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r3.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:18:28-29/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses faraṭ as exceeding the truth; following desire and excess explain the heedless heart and restate its condition.

TABATABAI:18:28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:18:28/r1.claim: Rāghib defines ṣabr as restraint under constraint and, more generally, holding oneself to what reason and religious law require or away from what they forbid.

TABATABAI:18:28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r2.claim: God’s “face” means His beautiful names and attributes through which people address and worship Him; the divine essence itself cannot be directly reached.

TABATABAI:18:28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r3.claim: Seeking God’s active attributes, such as mercy and favor, means seeking to be covered by them and become recipients of mercy, approval, and grace.

TABATABAI:18:28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r4.claim: Seeking non-active attributes such as knowledge, power, and majesty means drawing near by taking the humble, weak, and ignorant position appropriate before them.

TABATABAI:18:28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r5.claim: The author rejects interpretations that “His face” means approval, God’s essence through an omitted word, or simply turning toward God and seeking nearness.

TABATABAI:18:28/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r6.claim: Calling on God morning and evening is a metonym for continuing devotion, since mornings and evenings recur; interpreting it as the two daily prayers or obligatory prayers is unpersuasive.

TABATABAI:18:28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:18:28/r7.claim: The root of “pass beyond” carries the sense of overstepping, so “let not your eyes pass beyond them” means do not leave or overlook the poor believers for worldly adornment.

TABATABAI:18:28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:18:28/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says “pass” implicitly means that the eye shies away or rises above them; without that implication, the wording would need a direct object.

TABATABAI:18:28/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:28/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:28/r9.claim: God’s making a person heedless is punitive forgetfulness after stubborn opposition to truth, parallel to the later image of coverings on hearts and deafness in ears.

TABATABAI:18:29-31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r5.claim: A report says 18:28 was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf, who asked the Prophet to expel poor believers and draw Meccan notables near; it glosses heedlessness as sealing, remembrance as monotheism, desire as shirk, and excess as ignorance.

TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.speaker: سلمان
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.claim: Salman reports that influential converts, including ʿUyayna ibn Badr and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, asked the Prophet to remove shabby poor Muslims such as Salman and Abū Dharr; the passage then warned them of fire.

TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.claim: Al-Qummī gives a similar report naming only ʿUyayna ibn al-Ḥuṣayn; its Medina setting and related reports conflict with the passage’s Meccan context.

TABATABAI:18:29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:18:29/r1.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī reports that the morning-and-evening calling in 18:28 refers to prayer.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n36/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his explanation of this verse at 6:52.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n37/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari and Razi
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n37/r1.claim: They explain aghfalna as whom We have found heedless, which Asad says accords with Qur'anic doctrine.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n38/r1.claim: The phrase about the person's affair literally describes abandoning or transgressing every boundary of what is right.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n39/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n39/r1.claim: Razi explains az-zalimun, evildoers, in this context as those who reject the truth.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r1.claim: Suradiq literally means an awning or tent covering and here evokes the smoke walls surrounding sinners.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n40/r2.claim: The smoke-wall image stresses that the sinners cannot escape their suffering in the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The next section resumes the surah's opening: after the cave story showed God helping those who serve His cause, the Prophet is told to keep reciting, direct guidance to poor companions, disregard wealthy opponents, and leave them their choice and fate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Furutan means exceeding limits or oppressing; the Prophet's concern for wealthy leaders aimed to spread religion, but he risked neglecting devout companions to court them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The stern address is not rebuke of the Prophet but of affluent, arrogant people who considered his companions inferior and demanded their exclusion before they would listen.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.claim: Quraysh elites said they would meet the Prophet if he dismissed poor believers; the verse warns against adopting their attitude.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.claim: Honor comes from faith and good character, not wealth; the Prophet should recite to all without favoring the rich, since God knows who benefits, and should remain earnestly with the poor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.claim: The same warning appears in 6:52: do not drive away those who call on God morning and evening seeking His favor.

QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.claim: Ghudwa and ghadāt both mean morning, with the former emphasizing a single morning act and the latter a time period.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r1.claim: The verse responds to prominent Makkans who would listen only if the Prophet sent away his poorer followers, and commands him to stay with sincere believers.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r2.claim: Calling upon God includes invoking, praising and glorifying Him, supplication, and performing prayers.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r3.claim: Morning and evening may specify the times of invocation or describe its constant practice.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r4.claim: Seeking God’s Face means seeking to please Him and earn His reward instead of earthly benefits; at the highest mystical level it can mean seeking a vision of God.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r5.claim: The Prophet must not look past the poor followers toward wealthier, influential potential followers or prefer the prominent over sincere, pious people.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r6.claim: The Prophet reportedly thanked God for letting him live until commanded to be patient with some men of his community.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r7.claim: The heedless person refers to the Makkans seeking the dismissal of the poorer followers.

STUDYQURAN:18:28/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:28/r8.claim: Their excess means prodigality, waste, and negligence, putting petty desires before truth.
